description: COACTUPC's date-edit engine on its VALID path - the case that owns the complete, successful traversal of all seven CSUTLDPY paragraphs across BOTH century arms, including the CSUTLDTC delegation that lives inside the copybook and is therefore missed by any program-level count of CALL sites. case10 owns the invalid branches; this case owns only the clean traversal. PROVENANCE (practice B12, AAP 0.7.6 risk R-A): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cpy/CSUTLDPY.cpy, app/cpy/CSUTLDWY.cpy, app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl, app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl and app/cpy-bms/COACTUP.CPY together with the decoded fixture rows, and was NOT captured from a live COBOL execution - executing the 28 legacy programs is impossible in this environment against eight independently verified blockers. No user-specified Rule governs this file: review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided", so enterprise best practice B1-B12 governs instead; no rule has been invented and the bar is not lowered. THE ENGINE AND ITS ORDER (gate G30, first matching condition wins). EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD [CSUTLDPY:L18] opens PESSIMISTICALLY with SET WS-EDIT-DATE-IS-INVALID TO TRUE [L19] and then falls through, in this order, to EDIT-YEAR-CCYY [L25], EDIT-MONTH [L91], EDIT-DAY [L150], EDIT-DAY-MONTH-YEAR [L209], EDIT-DATE-LE [L284] and, for the birth date only, EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH [L341]. Note the asymmetry preserved verbatim per practice B5: EDIT-YEAR-CCYY and EDIT-MONTH each set their flag NOT-OK first [L27, L92] and only reach ISVALID at the end [L86, L143], whereas EDIT-DAY sets FLG-DAY-ISVALID FIRST [L152]. Also preserved as written: the two statements stranded AFTER the EDIT-DATE-LE-EXIT. label - SET WS-EDIT-DATE-IS-VALID TO TRUE [L327] and its terminating period - which belong to the fall-through of EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD and are honoured rather than tidied. THE CSUTLDTC DELEGATION. EDIT-DATE-LE [L284-L323] does INITIALIZE WS-DATE-VALIDATION-RESULT [L290], MOVE 'YYYYMMDD' TO WS-DATE-FORMAT [L291], then CALL 'CSUTLDTC' USING WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD, WS-DATE-FORMAT, WS-DATE-VALIDATION-RESULT [L293-L296]. The first two arguments are X(8) while CSUTLDTC declares LS-DATE and LS-DATE-FORMAT as X(10) [app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:L84-L85], so BY REFERENCE widens both - the Java AccountDateValidator reproduces that as an explicit PIC X move to 10, giving '20141120  ' and 'YYYYMMDD  '. On this path WS-SEVERITY-N is 0, so the IF at [L298] CONTINUEs and the IF NOT INPUT-ERROR at [L318] sets FLG-DAY-ISVALID [L319]. In Java the call is account.AccountDateValidator delegating to util.DateUtilityJob, which despite its prompt-mandated name is a @Service and not a Spring Batch Job. THE 80-BYTE RESULT. WS-DATE-VALIDATION-RESULT [CSUTLDWY:L60-L85] is THIRTEEN spans, not twelve: WS-SEVERITY X(4) + FILLER X(11) 'Mesg Code:' + WS-MSG-NO X(4) + FILLER X(1) + WS-RESULT X(15) + FILLER X(1) + FILLER X(9) 'TstDate:' + WS-DATE X(10) + FILLER X(1) + FILLER X(10) 'Mask used:' + WS-DATE-FMT X(10) + FILLER X(1) + FILLER X(3), i.e. 4+11+4+1+15+1+9+10+1+10+10+1+3 = 80 at offsets 0/4/15/19/20/35/36/45/55/56/66/76/77. Each of the four dates returns WS-SEVERITY '0000', WS-MSG-NO '0000', WS-RESULT 'Date is valid  ' - the success token is FC-INVALID-DATE VALUE X'0000000000000000' [CSUTLDTC:L62, L130] - WS-DATE-FMT 'YYYYMMDD  ', and every FILLER literal present. WS-DATE carries a deliberate COBOL artefact: MOVE WS-DATE-TO-TEST TO WS-DATE [CSUTLDTC:L122] is a GROUP move over a variable-length item, so the ten bytes are the S9(4) BINARY halfword Vstring-length - 10, i.e. X'000A' - followed by only the FIRST EIGHT characters of LS-DATE. That 80-byte group is ASSERTED, not merely described: expectedMessages carries it FOUR times on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel - the width the model fixes at exactly 80 and the channel the twenty shipped CSUTLDTC cases use for this very group - once per driven date and in COACTUPC's own edit order, Open Date [L1478], Expiry Date [L1490], Reissue Date [L1503], Date of Birth [L1533], with the 75-byte WS-RETURN-MSG image last because it is what the turn finally left behind. Each text is composed span by span from the thirteen PICTURE clauses rather than pasted as one opaque blob (practices B8 and B11), so every FILLER literal - 'Mesg Code: ', 'TstDate: ', 'Mask used:' and the two trailing space spans - is present at its declared width. The internal flag trio FLG-YEAR-ISVALID / FLG-MONTH-ISVALID / FLG-DAY-ISVALID is WORKING-STORAGE with no channel of its own in this model, so it is asserted through its two observable projections instead: no date field carries DFHRED in the attribute map, and no date message appears in the ordered message list - both of which are only true when all three flags reached LOW-VALUES and WS-EDIT-DATE-IS-VALID held. BOTH CENTURY ARMS IN ONE CASE. The three account dates are century 20 and exercise 88 THIS-CENTURY VALUE 20 [CSUTLDWY:L9]: ACCT-OPEN-DATE 2014-11-20, ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE 2025-05-20 (the copybook's misspelling is preserved, practice B3) and ACCT-REISSUE-DATE 2025-05-20. CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD 1961-06-08 is century 19 and exercises 88 LAST-CENTURY VALUE 19 [L10]; because it is valid, [COACTUPC:L1539-L1543] also performs EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH, whose INTEGER-OF-DATE comparison [L345-L350] passes against the pinned 2022-07-19 clock. Every date arrives as three separate components - OPNYEARI/OPNMONI/OPNDAYI X(4)/X(2)/X(2) and the EXP*, RIS*, DOB* triples per app/cpy-bms/COACTUP.CPY - never as a hyphenated string; the program assembles them into the 8-byte WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD. REACHING THE EDITS AT ALL. This is the post-fetch turn: it is the genuine successor of case04, whose outbound navigation image this case's inbound commarea reproduces byte for byte, with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1 and the change action carried as ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS 'S'. So [L1433] is false and the search-key-only shortcut at [L1435-L1446] is not taken. The trap is the next gate: 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS performs 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW [L1460] and then, IF NO-CHANGES-FOUND, MOVEs LOW-VALUES to WS-NON-KEY-FLAGS and GO TOes the exit [L1463-L1468] BEFORE any field edit runs. THE MINIMAL CHANGE INTRODUCED, and why: RISDAYI is 21 where the stored ACCT-REISSUE-DATE day is 20 - exactly one operator edit, which makes ACUP-NEW-REISSUE-DATE differ from ACUP-OLD-REISSUE-DATE in the account block at [L1694], sets CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED [L1703] and so defeats the short-circuit. It is deliberately a DATE that differs, because that is what proves the engine validates the RECEIVED value rather than the stored one, and 2025-05-21 is itself valid (May is a WS-31-DAY-MONTH [CSUTLDWY:L21-L23]). TWO PROPERTIES OF THIS SEED THAT THE READER MUST NOT MISTAKE FOR DEFECTS. First, the short-circuit would in fact already be defeated without any operator edit: 1100-RECEIVE-MAP maps AADDGRPI = '*' OR SPACES to LOW-VALUES [L1213-L1215] while the stored ACCT-GROUP-ID is ten spaces, so the TRIM/UPPER-CASE group-id term at [L1697-L1700] differs on every re-submission of this account - which is also why AADDGRPO is pinned as ten LOW-VALUES rather than ten spaces [L2921]. The explicit reissue-day edit is retained regardless, so that the change this case rests on is stated rather than incidental. Second, the stored customer CANNOT pass COACTUPC's full edit suite: CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE is 274 and 1275-EDIT-FICO-SCORE requires 300 to 850, and behind it the state/zip cross-field check [L1280] and the phone-2 area code also fail. No screen for this seed can therefore be error-free without fabricating field values, which practices B11 and B12 forbid; every payload byte here instead traces to a fixture byte or a PICTURE clause, with the single deliberate day shift as the one exception. THE RESIDUAL MESSAGE IS EVIDENCE, NOT NOISE. WS-RETURN-MSG is only ever assigned under IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF, so ONLY THE FIRST failing edit's text sticks. The three account dates are edited at [L1478-L1507] and the birth date at [L1533-L1543], all BEFORE FICO at [L1545-L1556]. The message therefore being the FICO text - and NO date message - positively proves that not one of the four date edits failed, and the attributes say the same thing from the other side: ACSTFCOC, ACSSTTEC, ACSZIPCC and ACSPH2AC are DFHRED while NO date field is reddened. INFOMSGH is DFHBMASB per [L3567-L3571] and FKEY12H is DFHBMASB because ACUP-CHANGES-MADE holds and ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE does not [L3573-L3576]. OUTCOME. Because INPUT-ERROR is set by that later FICO edit, [L1671-L1675] leaves the change action at ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK 'E' rather than promoting it to ACUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, so 2000-DECIDE-ACTION takes WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK -> CONTINUE [L2596-L2597], 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG takes WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK -> PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES [L2964-L2965, literal at L470-L471], and the cursor EVALUATE lands on the FICO field. The transaction returns to itself pseudo-conversationally. NOTHING IS WRITTEN: expectedWrites is empty and all four datasets are asserted unchanged at their copybook widths 300/500/150/50, which is correct because this turn reaches no file verb at all - 2000-DECIDE-ACTION only reads on its ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED / PFK12 arm [L2568-L2580]. RETURN CODE 0: COACTUPC sets no COBOL RETURN-CODE on any path. CSUTLDTC's own MOVE WS-SEVERITY-N TO RETURN-CODE [CSUTLDTC:L98] is internal to that subprogram and is asserted by CSUTLDTCParityTest, not here. GATES: G15, G16 (cardxref seeded RAW at 36 bytes and padded to 50 by the declared normalisation), G18, G30, G37 (no server-side state - the commarea, the AID and every screen value travel in the payload), G51 (unit kind CONTROLLER_POJO: account.AccountUpdateController built through its own constructor with the real account.AccountDateValidator and util.DateUtilityJob injected - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no JobLauncher). NON-APPLICABLE, STATED EXPLICITLY: G32 does not apply because CBSTM03A is the only program with backward loop-forming GO TOs and this is not it, and G35 does not apply because COACTUPC contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and this path raises no AbendException.
